name: Tahash
overview: Tahash is a male biblical figure identified as a son of Nahor through his concubine Reumah, as recorded in Genesis 22:24. Beyond this unique lineage detail, Scripture does not provide further information about his tribe or additional attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Tahash is a proper name mentioned in Genesis 22:24 and is understood to mean a species of dolphin. There is no indication that this name was given by God or carries additional theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Tahash as a son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, through Reumah, Nahor’s concubine. These are the only family relationships noted in the biblical text regarding Tahash.
scriptureSignificance: Tahash’s significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the family of Nahor, connecting him to the broader narrative of Abraham’s extended family. His mention underscores the biblical practice of recording descendants, including those born to concubines, which reflects the comprehensive nature of God’s providential care over families in the patriarchal period.
